subject: Dedicated SKU plan: staged H100→A100→L4 concession roadmap for Marbles AI
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Eva Martinez <eva@marbles.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 09:23:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated SKU plan: staged H100→A100→L4 concession roadmap for Marbles AI

Eva —

Thanks again for the sync this morning. Per our conversation, I sketched a pragmatic path that lets Marbles keep high-memory capacity for the early long-context experiments while giving you a clear runway to reduce unit cost once quantized models and batching are proven in-production.

High level recommendation (pilot → steady-state):
- Phase 0 (pilot, 0–6 weeks): Anchor with memory-heavy nodes so your 50k+ token evaluation runs reliably.
  - Start: 6x H100 (dense long-context slots), 8x A100 (balanced inference & burst), 16x L4 (low-latency embeddings/baseline throughput)
- Phase 1 (concession window, 6–12 weeks): Move non-critical inference and pre/post-processing to A100/L4 as prompts are optimized and KV caching is working. Target ~30% workload shift to L4.
- Phase 2 (steady-state, 3+ months): Evaluate measured accuracy delta and cost per request. If memory utilization stays <60% on H100 slots and model quantization passes QA, shift further to A100/L4 mix to optimize $/token.

Key tradeoffs we considered:
- Memory headroom: H100 gives the largest safety margin for 50k–70k token contexts; A100 can work with aggressive tiling/kv-slicing but needs more orchestration.
- Tail latency: L4 provides better 99th pct for short requests, but will not support very large KV caches — use it for embeddings, reranking, and short-form responses.
- Cost/slot: L4 << A100 < H100; but the functional delta for long-context generation can be non-linear.

Operational concessions and guardrails (what we propose to make procurement comfortable):
- Time-based concession windows tied to objective metrics (accuracy regressions <1.5% and token cost improvement >=20%).
- Auto-fallback policy: if a long-context generation route detects OOMs or >3x latency regression, requests automatically route back to H100 variants.
- Monthly telemetry checkpoint with Redwood to rebench model perf after quantization/compilation changes.

I've attached the workload snapshot you shared (marbles_workload_snapshot_Q2.xlsx) and a short runbook that maps monitoring thresholds to capacity moves (sku_concession_runbook.pdf).

Next steps I suggest:
1) Approve pilot slotting so we can reserve capacity for the onboarding week (May 10).
2) Agree on the two KPIs that will trigger the Phase 1 shift (recommended: 28-day mean memory utilization + quantized accuracy on holdout set).

If you want, Ben can put together a quick cost projection at the per-10k token level for the three-node classes.

—Irene

Subject: Re: Dedicated SKU plan: staged H100→A100→L4 concession roadmap for Marbles AI

Thanks, Irene — this is helpful. A couple quick clarifying questions before we commit budget:
1) Our largest model runs ~70k tokens in peak experiments. How much buffer should we plan per H100 to avoid OOM during A/B testing?
2) The procurement team is asking for an expected delta in monthly committed spend between pilot and steady-state if we hit the 30% shift to L4. Can Ben quantify "expected spend" by May 3?

Also, are there specific metrics you want us to provide from our end (trace samples, p99 latency distributions, quantization evals) to accelerate the concession decision?

—Eva
Eva Martinez, Head of Infrastructure
Marbles AI
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Eva Martinez <eva@marbles.ai>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 09:50:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated SKU plan: staged H100→A100→L4 concession roadmap for Marbles AI

Eva — quick answers and a rough cost sketch attached.

1) H100 headroom: for a 70k token peak we recommend provisioning ~20% headroom per H100 slot (KV cache + model activations). Practically that means 6 H100 slots will sustain ~+20% burst beyond your current peak testing envelope. If you want an extra safety buffer for the first two weeks, we can reserve a hot spare H100 to avoid mid-pilot shifts.

2) Cost delta (pilot vs steady-state): rough numbers (monthly committed) — assumptions in attached spreadsheet:
- Pilot (6 H100, 8 A100, 16 L4): est committed spend = $98k/month
- Steady-state target mix (4 H100, 10 A100, 28 L4): est committed spend = $73k/month
- Estimated savings if 30% of inference volume shifts to L4 ≈ 25% lower $/token across the fleet (details in marbles_cost_breakdown tab).

What we need from you to make Phase 1 go/no-go decisions:
- p99 latency sample for representative user traffic (one week)
- A small quantization sweep results (FP16→INT8/4) with accuracy delta on the holdout set (simple CSV)
- Any batching constraints (max tokens per request average)

I attached a short runbook (sku_concession_runbook.pdf) and the cost sketch (marbles_workload_snapshot_Q2.xlsx updated with cost tab). If you can ping procurement that you'd like Redwood's finance team to present the committed vs burst pricing on May 3, we can lock pilot slots that day.

Ben Carter
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
